notes: Both verbless clauses put the copula on the predicate and leave the explicit pronoun only its own English (rule 20): *art* on `אֱלוֹהָי`, discontinuous around the possessive, and *is* on `טוֹבָה`.
Both marginal notes — *Let thy good Spirit lead me* and *a plain country* — were read and set aside; the printed text governs (rule 38).

The supplied *the* of *the land* goes to the construct noun under rule 29, no article morpheme standing in the phrase, and *of uprightness* to the rectum under rule 19. Nothing is added or unrepresented.
